clue.text: Brown bear, one captured by photographer?

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the photographer's name, as a prisoner is captured

parts.note: Kodak, the camera and film maker, stands for a photographer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cameraman snaps a brown bear in the wild and wonders if he has caught one on film.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodiak is a large subspecies of brown bear from the islands of Alaska.

clue.text: Action of intruder, maybe, to go and test the system?

parts.note: to go, as a euphemism, is to pee
to ping is to send a test signal to a computer system to check it responds

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a trespasser's move is simply to probe the security set-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeping Tom intrudes on privacy, so spying through windows is an intruder's typical activity.

clue.text: I'm disgusted, mate — raised parts look carelessly executed

indicators.note: the reversed words split the word for look into two parts, sitting between them

parts.note: to spy is to look

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pah is an exclamation of disgust
a pal is a mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A disgusted onlooker tells a friend that the lifted sections look sloppily made.
explanation.walkthrough: Being a down clue, 'raised' turns both words upwards, and 'parts' means they split the word for look in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaphappy means casual or slapdash, describing work done in a careless, haphazard way.

clue.text: Tragic high-flier over island carried off great singer

indicators.note: the island letter is carried away, removed from the high-flier's name

parts.note: Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell to his death
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A doomed aviator flying over an island is swept away, a great singer lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Malicious desire to cut through

indicators.note: the word for desire cuts into the word for through, splitting it apart

parts.note: by means through, as in 'by means of'
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: A spiteful urge to slash through something.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitchy is informal for spiteful and catty, saying unkind things to hurt someone.

clue.text: British pairs introducing young woman to dance

indicators.note: the two pairs bring in the young woman, placing her between them

parts.note: in cricket a pair is two ducks, OO, so pairs are two of those
gal is a young woman

explanation.surface: British couples bring a girl to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a pair is a batter's score of nought in both innings, so a pair is two ducks, two zeros.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogaloo is a 1960s dance style with roots in Latin and soul music.

clue.text: Curried with lamb or chicken heart, some say

indicators.note: what some people say aloud sounds like the word meant

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A curry made with lamb, or chicken heart, so some people claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka describes Indian dishes of marinated meat pieces, as in chicken tikka or lamb tikka.

clue.text: Play, yes, on fine castle walls

indicators.note: the castle encloses the other letters like walls

parts.note: Hever Castle in Kent was the childhood home of Anne Boleyn

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A theatrical production staged within the grounds of a castle on a fine day, everyone agreeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay Fever is a 1924 comedy by Noël Coward, so it names a stage work.

clue.text: On the other side of boxes reveal rum

indicators.note: the two letters of the word of box in the rearranged letters
rum means odd or strange, so the letters are made odd by reordering

explanation.surface: A strange revelation hidden inside some containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Overleaf means on the reverse of the page, the other side of the sheet.

clue.text: "East Londoner! Not North — East!" (One looks askance.)

indicators.note: not here means without, so the north letter is dropped

parts.note: a Cockney is a native of London's East End
N is the compass abbreviation for north
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A shout correcting a direction: not north but east, from a squinting Londoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockeye is a squinting eye, one that looks sideways rather than straight.

clue.text: So new setters to debut soon? First signs of interference, Notabilis packs up!

definitions.text: So new setters to debut soon?

indicators.note: the first signs of each word are their opening letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crossword announcement: new compilers are about to appear, as the Notabilis byline signals with interference.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters are dogs here, Irish or English setters, so new setters are puppies yet to be born. Notabilis is a fellow crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitch in pup is pregnant, so her puppies are due to be born soon.

clue.text: Device filling patisserie twists?

indicators.note: twists means the words are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: mega means huge or substantial, as a filling meal is
tarts are patisserie, pastries

explanation.surface: A gadget for putting the filling into twisted pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or ploy, a device to outwit someone.

clue.text: Bell the cat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Great ... is the large bell of Christ Church, Oxford

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell the cat' is the fable of mice wanting to hang a bell on a cat; here the bell and the cat are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is used for a large bell, Great Tom at Oxford, and for a male cat.

clue.text: On a rag, drunk punches floor bouncer?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters punch into the knockout letters, landing inside them

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling and out of order

explanation.surface: A drunk on a spree throws a punch and knocks the doorman down.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo moves by hopping and bounding, so it is literally an animal that bounces.

clue.text: Discovered wanting eats great quantity!

indicators.note: discovered means the cover is stripped off, the outer letters removed

parts.note: foodless means lacking food, wanting eats

explanation.surface: Someone found to be short of food eats an enormous amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for lots, a very large amount of something.

clue.text: A curious entity passed over fast air travellers

parts.note: ob, from Latin obiit, means died, passed over
a jet and a dart both travel quickly through the air

explanation.surface: A strange being has flown past swift aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An objet d'art is an ornamental curio, a small article valued for its artistry.

clue.text: Last confidant of three people attending delivery

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators attending a match
the post is the mail delivered each day

explanation.surface: A third person brought in to a secret while three people attend a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'between you, me and the gatepost', a promise of secrecy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom about secrecy, the third party trusted with the secret after you and me is a gatepost.

clue.text: Secretary beginning to type perfectly

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A secretary starting to type flawlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something pat, or off pat, is to know it exactly, without hesitation.

clue.text: Supply church with song from the comfort of home

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Providing a church with a hymn while staying at home in comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or traveller acts only from their seat, without direct experience.

clue.text: A bit of old fish with it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shilling, a coin of old British money
second meaning: a float on an angler's line

explanation.walkthrough: A bob was the slang name for a shilling in pre-decimal British money; it is also a fishing float.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old shilling coin and an angler's float.

clue.text: Creative expression feeds my right to torture

indicators.note: the word for creative expression is fed into the middle of my

parts.note: art is creative expression

explanation.surface: Art nourishes my right to inflict pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To martyr someone can mean to inflict great suffering on them, to torment or persecute.

clue.text: Little boy finally arrives after midnight

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

parts.note: am, ante meridiem, covers the hours after midnight

explanation.surface: A child at last gets home in the early hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam is a common boy's name, so a little boy may be called that.

clue.text: One supplies handle if giving him a lift?

definitions.text: One supplies handle if giving him a lift?

indicators.note: in a down clue a lift raises the letters so they read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a namer supplies a handle, a name

explanation.surface: A wry note that the man who carries you might ask your name first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also points at the fireman's lift, a way of carrying someone over the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A firefighter is known for the fireman's lift, carrying a person across the shoulders.

clue.text: What follows cake-maker's topping in glace fancy?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine, so the letters are reimagined in a new order
what follows the topping, the first letter of cake-maker's, is its second letter

explanation.surface: Asking what comes next on top of a fancy iced cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' does double duty: the definition, and the C at the top of 'cake-maker's', which the A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied angelica stems are used to decorate cakes and trifles.

clue.text: Her habits apparently unbesmirched ahead of vows?

definitions.text: Her habits apparently unbesmirched ahead of vows?

parts.words: Her habits apparently unbesmirched ahead of vows?
parts.note: a trainee nun wears habits, and splitting the answer gives a phrase meaning no wrongdoing, before taking final vows

explanation.walkthrough: Habits are both a nun's robes and patterns of behaviour; split as NO VICE the answer says those habits are clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationer in a religious order who has not yet taken final vows.

clue.text: Taken in by Ximeneans, we revealed what to write in

indicators.note: the letters are taken inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Followers of Ximenes reveal what to fill in on the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximeneans are solvers and setters who follow Ximenes' strict rules of clueing.
explanation.definitionFit: In a crossword the solver writes the solution, the entry that fills the lights, into the grid.

clue.text: Singer's given a funky city room that overlooks it

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a head

indicators.note: funky suggests the letters are jazzed up and shuffled
the letters of it are overlooked, left out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A singer is given a trendy urban room with a view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' is 'Singer is'; the anagram of CITY ROOM leaves out IT to give RYCOMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry Como was an American crooner and television entertainer of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Between tracks, it's broadcast in splendid style!

indicators.note: the spoken letters sit between the railway letters

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, tracks

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, so the word is spelt as it sounds

parts.note: it's said aloud is spelt ITZ

explanation.surface: Between music tracks, a radio show goes out with great flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy means luxurious and glamorous, like the Ritz hotel, an adjective of lavish style.

clue.text: Force releases universal order

indicators.note: releases means lets go of the letter, removing it

parts.note: duress is compulsion, force
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A military force sets free a worldwide command.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress ranks is to put soldiers in order, aligning them in a line.

clue.text: No stamp? That would rile him

definitions.text: No stamp? That would rile him

indicators.note: to rile is to stir up and agitate, so the letters of the first two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An unstamped letter would annoy the person who has to deliver it.
explanation.definitionFit: The mail carrier must deliver letters, and one lacking postage causes him trouble.

clue.text: Muffler used by wicked gangster

parts.note: a muffler is a scarf
wicked and ace are both slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A villain uses a muffler to disguise himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of Al Capone and the title of gangster films.

clue.text: The Old Sun, is it, accommodating paying guest?

indicators.note: the heavenly body accommodates the old word, holding it inside

parts.note: the Sun is a star
ye is an old spelling of the

explanation.surface: A query about whether the Old Sun inn is putting up a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is it' questions the Sun as a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is one who stays, like a lodger or guest paying for a room.
